Start with the bottleneck

Choose the work before the marketing company

A launch can fill a Discord server and still leave a product without customers. A busy press calendar can produce little pipeline. Before choosing an agency, decide what a useful next action looks like for your buyer: a developer ships an integration, a company books a qualified meeting, or a customer returns after a first transaction. Those are different growth jobs.

Web3 marketing combines familiar disciplines with wallet-based journeys, token incentives, technical audiences and channel restrictions. It does not replace positioning, product usability or customer support. If visitors abandon onboarding, sending more traffic into that journey may amplify the problem. Give candidates your actual funnel and ask what they would fix before buying reach.

For an RWA issuer, an eligible investor enquiry is not the same as a completed subscription. For an RPC platform, a new API key is not the same as an active production integration. For a game, a reward claim is not the same as a returning player. Write these distinctions into the brief so suppliers cannot quietly substitute a larger but less useful number.

Compare the scope

What Web3 marketing services should include

Brand, positioning and creative

Ask who the product serves, why it is different and what the audience must understand before acting. Request message architecture, landing pages, design assets and an approval process. A visual refresh alone does not resolve an unclear product promise. Confirm ownership of source files, licenses, voice guidelines and accessibility checks.

PR and communications

Separate story development, media pitching, executive preparation, press-release distribution and commercial placement. Ask which outcomes are earned, purchased or syndicated. Count original coverage separately from copies and keep publication dates and URLs in the report. Include correction and incident procedures; a journalist relationship is not control over an editorial decision.

Creators and KOL campaigns

Screen audience geography, topic relevance, engagement patterns and previous promotions. Request the named creator, deliverable, approval rights, disclosure plan and post-campaign evidence. Agree treatment of deleted posts, missed dates, fabricated engagement and competing promotions. A large follower count is not evidence that the audience will use your product.

Community and social operations

Define coverage hours, languages, response targets, moderator permissions and escalation. Separate education and support from promotional posting. Use client-controlled administrator accounts, secure access and a scam-response process. Never ask community staff to handle seed phrases. Include a launch-week plan for impersonation, malicious links and overwhelmed support queues.

SEO, content and AI discovery

Request a topic and intent map, original source research, clear authorship and an update policy. Technical work should check indexability, canonical URLs, sitemap accuracy, redirects and usable page rendering. Measure citations separately from search rank and traffic. Preserve the exact prompt, date, engine and cited URL when testing answers; one appearance does not establish persistent visibility.

Paid acquisition and CRO

Require a product-and-market eligibility check before planning media. Confirm targeting, placements, creative variants, landing pages and events. Test the real form on mobile, including ordinary website-address formats and error recovery. Count only accepted submissions or confirmed backend outcomes as successful leads, and reconcile analytics with the lead store.

Events, partners and developer programs

Start with the people you need to meet and the product action you want afterward. Separate sponsorship from editorial or speaking selection. For hackathons, distinguish registrations, submitted projects and maintained integrations. Agree consent-based lead capture, duplicate handling, sales follow-up and a post-event review instead of treating badge scans as opportunities.

Lifecycle, email and retention

Map onboarding, education, activation, return visits and re-engagement. Specify consent, suppression and unsubscribe handling, delivery ownership and the CRM handoff. Segment technical users, institutions and retail audiences rather than sending one message to everyone. Review whether users stay after rewards expire and whether sales teams accept the enquiries generated.

Choose the operating model

Agency, fractional leader, internal team or software?

Compare responsibility, not labels
ModelUseful whenResponsibility to allocate
Multi-channel agencySeveral channels must run on one coordinated calendarNamed strategy lead, execution team, approvals, dependencies and reporting
Specialist agencyOne bottleneck needs focused expertiseHandoffs to your other suppliers, channel boundaries and integration with the wider plan
Fractional marketing leaderThe team needs senior direction without a full-time appointmentWho executes creative, media, content and operations after strategy is agreed
Internal teamThe product needs sustained knowledge and daily decision ownershipHiring, management, specialist capacity and continuity
Quest or community softwareYou need a specific engagement or access workflowCampaign design, administration, support, rewards and data exports
Publisher, network or eventYou need an agreed distribution productInventory, audience, labeling, dates, rights and measurement

A subscription, retainer, launch package and performance-linked agreement are commercial models, not proof of quality. Define the unit of delivery, named capacity, review cadence and exclusions. Performance incentives can reward the wrong behavior if the metric is easy to inflate. If compensation depends on leads or wallets, agree acceptance rules, duplicate treatment and quality review before launch.

Ask who actually does the work, which tasks are subcontracted and who covers absence or turnover. Global delivery does not mean local-language expertise, round-the-clock support or permission to market every product in every country. Request the working hours, markets and language reviewers for your campaign, not just a map of offices.

Measure what matters

From impressions to retained customers

Build a small measurement contract before the first campaign. For every metric record its definition, data source, owner, time zone, attribution window and exclusions. Agree whether a wallet, account, company or person is the unit. Multiple wallets can belong to one person; one account can represent a team. Do not report those units interchangeably.

A buyer-ready measurement specification
MetricCalculation or definitionLimit to disclose
Qualified lead rateSales-accepted enquiries divided by eligible submitted enquiriesState duplicate, spam, geography and eligibility exclusions
Activation rateEligible acquired accounts completing the agreed product action divided by eligible acquired accountsDefine the action and observation window before the campaign
Acquisition costAgreed attributable acquisition costs divided by accepted new activationsState whether creative, agency work, tools and incentives are included
RetentionAn acquisition cohort returning for a qualifying action in a stated later windowUse the same cohort denominator; separate rewarded and unrewarded users
Onchain activityQualifying transactions or funded accounts under documented filtersRemove test and internal activity; show bot and Sybil assumptions
TVL or asset growthExplain deposits, withdrawals, token-price effects and measurement timeAsset-price appreciation or recycled capital is not automatically marketing impact
PR outcomesOriginal relevant coverage, referral sessions and attributable enquiriesDo not add syndicated copies or potential publisher audiences as unique reach
AI citation observationA recorded answer citing a specific URL for a fixed promptRecord engine, locale, date and answer evidence; citations are not visits or sales

Connect browser events to real submissions

Use a consistent campaign naming convention and preserve source parameters through redirects and forms. Keep personally identifying information out of URLs and analytics events. A form-start event, validation error and successful server response should be different events. Confirm accepted records in your lead store and notification delivery independently, since an email outage does not necessarily mean storage failed.

Report unattributed conversions as unknown rather than assigning them to the most flattering channel. Consent choices, browser restrictions, cross-device journeys, shared links and missing tags can limit attribution. Direct traffic alone does not prove bots. Investigate landing pages, interaction patterns, server records and accepted leads before reaching a conclusion.

Test incrementality instead of claiming causation

A public dashboard can corroborate dates and activity but cannot isolate an agency's contribution from product launches, market movement or other campaigns. Where practical, compare a holdout, staggered rollout or matched cohort and document limitations. If no controlled comparison is possible, label the result as observed association. Keep the original baseline so later reports do not redefine success.

Run a post-incentive review

For quests, referrals and airdrops, compare rewarded activity with later product use after the reward window closes. Review repeated funding paths, unusually fast completions and duplicated behavior without assuming a wallet automatically identifies a person. Agree an appeal process for wrongly excluded participants. A smaller retained cohort can be more useful than a very large reward-claim total.

Check the evidence

How to read a marketing case study

Ask for a relevant example with a named product, campaign dates, starting point, measurement definition and supplier role. Was the engagement strategy, execution, media buying or a single creator introduction? What else launched at the same time? Request permissioned evidence or a reference rather than asking a supplier to disclose another client's confidential data.

Coinbound's current Web3 page describes Sui creator campaigns, Gala earned-media work and a MetaMask launch. Lunar Strategy's current site presents ecosystem, creator, event and developer case studies. Those examples help you ask about comparable work; the public claims do not establish that the same team, conditions or outcome will apply to you. This guide deliberately does not convert agency-reported headline numbers into forecasts.

  1. Identify the client and the product version at the time.
  2. Record the campaign and reporting dates, not just the publication date.
  3. Request the baseline, denominator, geography and audience definition.
  4. Separate paid media, rewards, organic distribution and existing customers.
  5. Ask what the agency controlled and what another team delivered.
  6. Check whether outputs are clicks, registrations, activations, qualified opportunities or retained users.
  7. Request source evidence and understand consent, access and attribution limits.
  8. Speak to a relevant client reference where permission is available.

Directory ratings can help identify questions, but platforms use their own verification and placement methods. Do not transplant review scores into a different scoring system. Missing public case-study figures do not prove inability; ask for an appropriate reference or scoped pilot. Equally, awards and client logos do not establish who delivered the work or whether the relationship is current.

Protect the campaign

Platform eligibility, claims and audience safeguards

Advertising permission depends on the actual product, advertiser and market. Google's cryptocurrency advertising policy distinguishes allowed, restricted and prohibited categories and location-specific certification. Do not assume a generic crypto certificate opens every channel. Require the supplier to document the intended campaign's eligibility before committing media and to track policy changes during delivery.

Microsoft Advertising's cryptocurrency application says approval is required for cryptocurrency-related advertising and that applying does not guarantee approval. Platform acceptance is separate from legal obligations. Do not evade restrictions with misleading landing pages, cloaked redirects or substitute advertiser identities.

The FTC's endorsement resources explain disclosure of material brand relationships and genuine review practices. Allocate creator briefing, disclosure review, monitoring and correction responsibilities. Avoid fake testimonials, engagement purchases and review suppression. Keep a dated record of approved creative and changes.

For UK-facing campaigns, consult the FCA's cryptoasset marketing resources with the responsible legal and compliance team. Other markets and products require their own review. This is a campaign-planning checklist, not an opinion that a particular promotion is lawful. A marketing agency, Vetted badge or platform approval does not substitute for the appropriate professional assessment.

Keep control of your assets and audience

Agree client ownership or continuing access for domains, ad accounts, analytics, pixels, CRM records, social channels and creative source files. Use named access with appropriate permissions, not shared passwords. Allocate consent, retention, deletion and cross-border data questions with the responsible specialists. Do not place personal data or wallet-to-person mappings on public dashboards.

Require a termination handover: campaigns and commitments, creative rights, raw reports, account access, suppression lists and open customer issues. Agree who can pause a campaign during a product incident or misleading promotion, who approves the correction and how evidence is preserved. A campaign that cannot be stopped safely is not ready to scale.

From brief to delivery

A practical first-quarter work plan

Illustrative milestones, not a promised growth forecast
StageWork to agreeEvidence at review
Before appointmentAudience, bottleneck, current funnel, markets and product constraintsWritten brief, roles, baseline, exclusions and acceptance rules
Initial setupTracking, access, positioning, form tests and channel eligibilityEvent specification, account ownership and approved claims
First controlled campaignsSmall tests across the selected channelsCreative and placement log, spend reconciliation and accepted outcomes
Cohort reviewReview quality, attribution gaps, sales feedback and repeat useCohort report and decision log explaining what to stop or change

A token event may need a fixed launch calendar; an enterprise product may need a longer sales cycle. Plan for product delays, policy rejection, creator changes and support capacity. Include a pre-launch pause decision and a post-launch servicing owner. Do not confuse a date-driven publicity milestone with a validated acquisition channel.

A proposal checklist you can reuse

  1. What precise audience and business problem will this engagement address?
  2. Who is the accountable lead, and who executes each channel?
  3. Which comparable engagement can we discuss with a reference?
  4. Which deliverables, languages, territories and hours are included?
  5. Who supplies product facts, technical review and legal approval?
  6. What is a qualified outcome, and which data source confirms it?
  7. How will spam, duplicates, incentives and attribution limits be reported?
  8. Which media, creator, tool and reward commitments require separate approval?
  9. Who owns accounts, creative rights, audience data and exports?
  10. How are changes, delays, failed placements and cancellations handled?
  11. What would trigger a pause, channel change or end to the engagement?
  12. What happens to operations, access and open leads at handover?

Compare replies side by side. Mark answers as evidenced, proposed or still open in your internal decision record. Do not reward a supplier for promising every channel. A clear exclusion with a sensible handoff is more useful than an unsupported claim of universal expertise.

Questions buyers ask

Web3 marketing agency FAQs

What is a Web3 marketing agency?

A Web3 marketing agency plans or executes growth for blockchain products and businesses. Work can include positioning, content, search, PR, creators, community, paid acquisition and lifecycle campaigns. A quest platform, publisher or conference is a different supplier with different responsibilities.

Which Web3 marketing agency is best?

Start with the audience and bottleneck, not a universal ranking. Compare named teams, relevant work, channel scope, accountable deliverables and measurement. A PR specialist, fractional marketing leader and acquisition agency may each fit a different stage of the same company.

Are crypto marketing and Web3 marketing different?

The labels overlap. Crypto campaigns may focus on exchanges or token events, while Web3 also includes developer infrastructure, games and onchain applications. The product, intended users and actual service agreement matter more than the label.

Should I hire an agency, a fractional CMO or an internal team?

Use an agency for coordinated execution across agreed channels, a fractional leader for senior direction with separate execution capacity, or an internal team for sustained ownership. Identify who manages the work, supplies creative and data, and makes decisions before choosing the model.

How should Web3 marketing results be measured?

Define a qualified activation and a retention window, then report eligible people or accounts, attributed activity, costs, exclusions and data limitations. For B2B, connect enquiries to accepted opportunities. For onchain products, distinguish wallets, people, incentives and price-driven asset changes.

Can an agency guarantee token price, exchange listings or AI citations?

Do not treat those outcomes as controllable deliverables. Exchanges, markets, publishers and answer engines make their own decisions. Contract for the work and evidence the supplier controls, with clear acceptance criteria and review points.

Are Galxe, Zealy and Collab.Land marketing agencies?

They provide different community software workflows. Galxe and Zealy support quests or engagement; Collab.Land describes token-based membership verification. Confirm the selected product. Your team or a separate operator still needs to own strategy, administration, support and measurement.

How do I compare proposals without a misleading price table?

Compare the same scope, named staff, creative work, third-party media, creator payments, incentives, tooling and reporting. Separate pass-through commitments from management work and agree change control, cancellation and export terms. Request a current written proposal for your actual needs.

What should a Web3 marketing case study prove?

Request the client, product, dates, baseline, denominator, paid distribution, incentives, metric definition and the agency role. Ask for permitted source evidence or a reference. An onchain chart can show activity without proving that a particular agency caused it.

How long does Web3 marketing take?

Set milestones around the work: measurement setup, positioning, first controlled campaigns and cohort review. Search, enterprise sales and retained product usage have different feedback cycles. Agree review dates and dependencies rather than assuming one timeline or forecast fits every channel.
